title: mini ops experiment capture — afternoon runs
content:
Quick personal capture of afternoon micro-runs — trying to keep an easy-to-skim single-sheet for jotting small config changes and immediate results. Not for prod reports; stash here and transfer anything worth keeping to Confluence later.

Context: running short burst tests against the 7B quantized variant on a single A100 instance to validate batching + prefix cache behavior for a conversational workload. Goal is to confirm simple knobs before handing off to infra bench-run.

Columns: date | run_id | prompt_len | batch | quant| p50_ms | p95_ms | tokens_out | est_cost_usd | notes

2024-11-07 | R-237a | 64 | 1 | int8 | 32 | 78 | 120 | 0.0032 | baseline, cold-start, no kv cache
2024-11-07 | R-237b | 64 | 4 | int8 | 45 | 120 | 480 | 0.0089 | batching 4, tail latency jump; investigate batching threshold
2024-11-07 | R-238 | 128 | 2 | int4 | 40 | 95 | 240 | 0.0057 | int4 quality looks fine, slight p50 regress vs int8 for long prompts
2024-11-08 | R-243 | 32 | 8 | int8 | 27 | 68 | 960 | 0.0168 | high throughput; p95 still OK, watch token variance
2024-11-09 | R-251 | 64 | 4 | int8 + kv | 28 | 55 | 480 | 0.0061 | enabled local prefix cache — big p95 improvement for repeated prefixes
2024-12-03 | R-302 | 256 | 2 | int8 + kv | 62 | 120 | 300 | 0.0095 | long prompt hit memory pressure, noticed GC spikes (kernel logs)
2024-12-20 | R-331 | 64 | 4 | q4f16 | 50 | 112 | 480 | 0.0042 | q4f16 reduced cost; slight quality sniff (n-gram mismatch)
2025-01-09 | R-412 | 16 | 16 | int8 | 22 | 49 | 2560 | 0.0282 | stress test for burst autoscale; throughput good, small p50 tail

Interpretation notes (informal):
- kv cache: huge win when prompt prefixes repeat across requests — p95 drops 30–50% in some cases. Need a quick microtest harness that replays a mixture of 70% repeated prefixes, 30% unique.
- batching: small batches (2–4) seem a sweet spot for mixed-latency targets. Larger batch sizes (8+) push p95 up unless we accept longer queuing + higher throughput. Consider dynamic batch cap per-route.
- quantization: int4/q4f16 reduce cost noticeably. Watch for edge-case hallucination increases in int4 on long context. Flagging to QA for a 200-sample prompt set.
- memory/GPU pressure: long sequences (>=256) with kv caching can trigger kernel-level memory churn — log and capture dmesg next time.

Quick TODOs (one-liners):
- [ ] build 70/30 prefix-replay harness (owner: me) — target by 2025-01-20
- [ ] add run metadata to GH issue for R-302 (owner: Arjun) — attach kernel logs
- [ ] run 200-sample QA pass for int4 vs int8 (owner: Sana) — shortlist failure modes
- [ ] experiment with dynamic-batch cap in local inference config (owner: me)

Questions to resolve:
- How much does queueing time add to observed p95 vs pure model latency? Need to isolate scheduler vs kernel.
- Is there a simple heuristic for switching to kv-cache by route without adding heavy routing logic? (TTL + recent-prefix count?)

One-line summary for handoff: "Int8 + kv-cache gives best latency with acceptable cost; int4 worth for cold-batch offline jobs but requires QA for long contexts. Implement prefix-replay harness and attach kernel logs for long-context runs before scaling up."

Scratch notes (timestamps):
- 2024-11-07 14:12: noticed p95 jump on batching 4 — likely queue depth.
- 2024-11-09 10:03: kv cache reduced repeated-run p95 from 120ms to ~55ms.
- 2024-12-03 16:44: kernel OOM warning during 256-run — file saved to /tmp/kernel-dumps/R-302.log

If I get time later: dump sample outputs and do small BLEU-like overlap check for int4 vs int8 to quantify the quality delta (quick script, <100 lines).

End of sheet — keeping this sparse and action-focused. Move anything that looks stable to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks when ready.
